Two-dimensional CFD analysis was conducted to evaluate gas velocity behavior within the reformer under varying internal flow configurations. The modeling demonstrated that smaller flow passages lead to elevated gas velocities that reduce effective residence time for plasma- assisted reactions. These findings informed selection of an internal flow scale that balances residence time requirements with acceptable pressure loss. Parametric CFD analysis was performed to evaluate the relationship between internal flow scale and pressure loss through the reformer. The results showed that increasing the effective flow area significantly reduces pressure drop, enabling operation within acceptable pressure-loss limits for engine integration. The pressure drop falls below one percent when the diameter exceeds 2.5 inches. 2.3.4 Experimental Setup and Procedures Multi-Scale Experimental Testing A series of experiments were conducted to evaluate the plasma reformer across bench-scale, facility-scale, and engine-integrated configurations. At the laboratory scale, a controlled test system was constructed to quantify plasma behavior and gas-phase composition. Methane flow rates ranging from 1 to 50 SLPM were regulated with mass-flow controllers. A residual gas analyzer measured hydrogen and hydrocarbon concentrations under plasma-on and plasma-off conditions. Concurrent voltage and current traces were recorded using an oscilloscope to calculate instantaneous power and energy efficiency for each operating point.
